findings.reason: the section must state that the extraction is definitional and pin it with a byte-equivalence test (or say entity decoding is deliberately dropped), because as written its promised test passes while the digest content silently differs.
findings.text: §16 deletes `_AuthoredProseParser` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:168`), a ~100-line parser that decodes HTML entities through `handle_data`, drops `<script>`/`<style>` content via `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS`, and excludes the `<head>`, and replaces its remaining job with `strip_tags`, a `_TAG_RE.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "")` over raw slices — but the plan's own verification for the swap only asserts that the *sliced section set* equals the deleted parser's set, which is a test of section coverage, not of prose-text equivalence, while an entity such as the `—`/`§` that fill every section of this plan survives the regex and was decoded by the parser, so the two mechanisms do not produce the same prose bytes

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §16 replaces the one deep prose mechanism the package owns, `_AuthoredProseParser` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:168`), with a one-expression regex stripper and its own verification cannot show the substitution preserves the digest.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — §17 consolidates rather than forks: it hoists `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` into `reckon/_plan_html.py` (move, not copy), makes the store's collapse and the module's two inline identity reads (`_plan_html.py:379,861`) consume the hoisted derivation, and routes the three store validity grammars onto `reckon/_schema.is_section_identity`; the near-duplicates it leaves beside these — `evidence._section_key`, `ledger.normalize_section`, and `_schema.is_section_identity` (derivation vs validity) — are each distinguished in §16/§17 text with the reason they keep their own frame.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1478, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 adds one public definition (`strip_tags`) and states why nothing can be retired ("the identity digest and the prose walk keep their names"); §17 adds two (`plan_headings` and the machinery predicate) and states why the family cannot shrink ("the two public readers ... each keep callers outside this module"); both are consistent with the counter as read here — `definitions()` (`reckon/interface_counts.py:74`) yields only function and class nodes, so the two exported constants the design adds are genuinely uncounted, and §16 reuses the existing plan-review-missing refusal family rather than adding one.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §16 and §17 name the mechanisms they extend and each was opened and confirmed present: `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` and `structured_section_spans` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:44,94`), `_TAG_RE` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:1506`), `_SECTION_IDENTITY`/`section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:219,224,243`), the AST census `read_trees`/`definitions` (`reckon/interface_counts.py:74,441`), `is_implementable_section` (`reckon/_schema.py`, consumed by `reckon/roadmap.py:107`), and `read_plan_review` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:494`); the store helpers §17 moves (`_section_heading`, `_wrapper_section_heading`, `_landed_card_span`, `_H2_OPEN_RE`, `_SECTION_OPEN_RE`) all exist in `reckon/_store.py:848-1064`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two thin layers the design adds each state why they cannot be an extension inline: `strip_tags` (§16) exposes the module's existing `_TAG_RE` expression across the package boundary rather than adding a second tag expression, and the machinery-element predicate (§17) is the single owner the fourteen `"data-reckon"` sites converge onto rather than a parallel spelling.
